sense: a person, book or record that information comes from

terms.gloss: an informant, an authority; the writer one follows
terms.comment: A historian names his source with auctor est (see according to).

terms.gloss: a source (a work one draws on)
evidence: M-O s.v. source (a book or other work supplying information)
terms.comment: Classically a figure: to draw from the springs, not chase the rivulets (Cic. Ac. 1.8, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: quibus in extrēmīs erat sibi īnsidiās fierī; sē id certīs auctōribus comperisse
phrases.english: at the end of which he said that a plot was being laid against him, and that he had it from reliable sources

phrases.latin: tum mihi nōn dubiīs auctōribus incipit aestās
phrases.english: then, on no doubtful authority, my summer begins
